record.original_question: Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. Does there exist a function f_M, invariant under rescaling of M, with the following property: whenever a geodesic net G on M has total length L, adjusted length L_tilde, diameter D, and n unbalanced vertices, the number of balanced vertices is at most f_M(L_tilde, L/D, n)? Here the adjusted length L_tilde is obtained by summing over all edges e_i the arclength integral of 1 / inj(e_i(s)), where inj(e_i(s)) is the injectivity radius of M at the point e_i(s). In particular, if M has injectivity radius inj > 0, must the number of balanced vertices be at most f_M(L / inj, L / D, n)?

evidence.quote: The adjusted total length L̃ of a geodesic net is the sum of integrals over all edges ei parametrized by their respective arclengths of 1 / inj(ei(s)), where inj(ei(s)) denotes the injectivity radius of the ambient Riemannian manifold at ei(s).

Conjecture 3.4.3 (Boundedness conjecture for geodesic nets on Riemannian manifolds). Let M be a complete Riemannian manifold. There exists a function fM which depends on M but is invariant with respect to rescalings of M with the following property: Let G be a geodesic net on M with total length L, adjusted length L̃ and diameter D that has n unbalanced vertices. Then its number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L̃, L / D, n). In particular, if M has injectivity radius inj > 0, then the number of balanced vertices does not exceed fM (L / inj, L / D, n).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a complete Riemannian manifold. A geodesic net on $M$ is a finite graph $G$ immersed in $M$ such that every edge is a geodesic segment parametrized by arclength. A vertex $v$ of $G$ is called balanced if the sum of the unit tangent vectors along the edges incident to $v$, taken in the outgoing direction at $v$, equals zero; otherwise it is called unbalanced. Let $L$ denote the total length of $G$ (sum of the lengths of its edges) and let $D$ denote its diameter (the diameter of $G$ as a metric subspace of $M$). For a point $p \in M$, let $\mathrm{inj}(p)$ denote the injectivity radius of $M$ at $p$. Define the adjusted total length of $G$ by
$$\widetilde L \;=\; \sum_{i} \int_0^{\ell(e_i)} \frac{ds}{\mathrm{inj}(e_i(s))},$$
where the sum is over all edges $e_i$ of $G$, parametrized by arclength, and $\ell(e_i)$ is the length of $e_i$.

Question: Does there exist a function $f_M : \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0} \times \mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0} \to \mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}$, depending on $M$ but invariant under rescaling of the metric of $M$, such that for every geodesic net $G$ on $M$ with total length $L$, adjusted length $\widetilde L$, diameter $D$, and exactly $n$ unbalanced vertices, the number of balanced vertices of $G$ is at most $f_M(\widetilde L,\, L/D,\, n)$?

In particular, if $M$ has positive (global) injectivity radius $\mathrm{inj}(M) > 0$, must the number of balanced vertices of any geodesic net $G$ on $M$ with total length $L$, diameter $D$, and $n$ unbalanced vertices be bounded above by $f_M(L/\mathrm{inj}(M),\, L/D,\, n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: The conjecture appears to remain open. Subsequent work (e.g., constructions toward unbounded numbers of balanced vertices in geodesic nets with four boundary points, results on three-boundary-vertex configurations, and studies on flat spheres and non-compact manifolds) addresses related sub-problems but does not establish or refute the full boundedness conjecture in terms of $(\widetilde L, L/D, n)$ on general complete Riemannian manifolds. Recent (2024–2025) work suggests progress toward unboundedness for four boundary vertices, which could potentially constrain or disprove related boundedness statements, but no definitive resolution of this specific conjecture was found.

status_evidence.title: Towards Constructing Geodesic Nets with Four Boundary Vertices and an Increasing Number of Balanced Vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Constructions approaching geodesic nets with four boundary vertices and arbitrarily many balanced vertices.
status_evidence.claim: Recent progress toward unboundedness in a related setting suggests the boundedness question is still actively investigated and not resolved.

status_evidence.title: On the existence of a balanced vertex in geodesic nets with three boundary vertices
status_evidence.snippet: Each geodesic net with three unbalanced vertices on a non-positively curved Riemannian plane has at most one balanced vertex.
status_evidence.claim: Partial results exist for special cases (three unbalanced vertices), but the general conjecture remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Geodesic nets on non-compact Riemannian manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Studies of geodesic nets on non-compact Riemannian manifolds.
status_evidence.claim: Related work continues but does not settle the general boundedness conjecture.
